results.finding: English reader-facing readiness instruction is gender-neutral, but Latvian gatavs is masculine; revise it to remain gender-neutral while preserving meaning and protected navigation identities.
The label for Simplified Chinese is grammatically incomplete and unnatural in Latvian; use a complete idiomatic Latvian designation while preserving the linked native label and URL.
The completion sentence uses masculine pabeidzis for a gender-neutral reader; revise it to avoid assuming gender while preserving the meaning and navigation links.
The contrast beginning Atšķirībā no C valodā Go has defective Latvian syntax; make the C-versus-Go contrast grammatical without changing the explicit type-conversion claim.

The final C-versus-Go contrast has defective Latvian syntax; revise it into grammatical Latvian while preserving the exact claim that Go has no pointer arithmetic.

The heading capitalizes nil as an ordinary word and is not natural Latvian technical phrasing; represent the Go nil identity accurately and make the heading natural, leaving body and code occurrences unchanged.
The text calls the Go blank identifier underscore a variable, introducing a technical error; describe assignment to the blank identifier accurately while preserving the underscore and code examples.

The reader-facing image-choice sentence assumes masculine gender, and the containment phrase for each []uint8 inside [][]uint8 is overly literal; use gender-neutral, professional Latvian while preserving all code identities.

English “You finished this lesson!” is gender-neutral, but Latvian “Jūs esat pabeidzis šo nodarbību!” uses a masculine participle for the reader. Revise the completion message so it remains gender-neutral while preserving the meaning and navigation links.

The preferred glossary term for “pointer receiver” is rādītāja saņēmējs, but the heading and body use the inconsistent plural construction “rādītāju saņēmējiem / rādītāju saņēmējus”. This changes the modifier from the glossary's singular-genitive compound form and can read as “receivers of pointers”. Revise the inflected plural occurrences so the established pointer receiver terminology remains consistent throughout the Unit.

English “If you're not sure” is gender-neutral, but “Ja neesat pārliecināts” uses a masculine adjective for the reader. Revise this reader-facing parenthetical so it is gender-neutral without changing the instruction to continue to the next page.

The Go technical identity nil is rendered as capitalized plain-text “Nil” in both the heading and opening sentence. Go's nil identity is case-sensitive and should not become Nil merely because it begins a heading or sentence. Revise the prose structure as needed so the technical identity remains lowercase while the Latvian remains natural.

In the sentence corresponding to “A nil error denotes success”, the candidate begins with “Nil error”, capitalizing the Go technical identity nil. Revise the sentence so nil remains the correct lowercase identity while preserving the contrast between nil and non-nil error values.

English “You finished this lesson!” is gender-neutral, but Latvian “Jūs esat pabeidzis šo nodarbību!” uses a masculine participle for the reader. Revise the completion message so it remains gender-neutral while preserving the meaning and navigation links.

English says the sync primitives “won't need [to be used] much in Go as there are other primitives”, making a general statement about Go programming. The candidate changes this to “ceļvedī Go tie gandrīz nebūs vajadzīgi”, narrowing the claim to this Go tour/guide. This materially changes the teaching scope. Revise the sentence so it again states the intended general relationship within Go, without adding the tour-specific limitation.

In the translated teaching comment for v := <-ch, “piešķirt vērtību v” can mean “assign the value v” rather than the source meaning “assign the received value to v”. The recipient role of v is therefore unclear and the explanatory comment no longer precisely describes the code. Revise the comment so v is unambiguously the variable receiving the value, while preserving the code unchanged.

The first sentence “Select priekšraksts select...” is redundant and inconsistent with the preferred glossary form select priekšraksts; it effectively names the construct twice and leaves an unnecessary capitalized English Select in Latvian prose. Revise the sentence to use the established select statement terminology naturally while preserving the Go keyword select.

After “10 vērtības”, the sentence “Tiem jābūt skaitļiem...” has incorrect Latvian gender agreement: the pronoun does not agree with feminine plural vērtības. Revise the sentence so the reference to the ten received values is grammatically correct while retaining the required sequence 1 through 10.

The linked technical title “First Class Functions in Go” is translated as “Pirmšķirīgas funkcijas valodā Go”. In Latvian, pirmšķirīgas ordinarily means first-rate/excellent and does not accurately convey the programming concept “first-class” as a status/category of values. Revise the link label using established Latvian computing terminology that conveys the first-class-function concept, while preserving the link target and the rest of the sentence.

The comments for Inc and Value render “for the given key” as “dotās key”, producing an unnatural mixed Latvian/English grammatical construction around the identifier key. The source refers to the key associated with the counter, while the current wording does not form idiomatic professional Latvian. Revise both comments so this relationship is expressed naturally in Latvian while preserving any required identifier identity and without changing the Go code.
